title: Farm-to-Table Local Board
seo_title: Farm-to-Table Charcuterie Board: Local Shopping Guide (8–12)
description: A farm-to-table charcuterie board for 8–12: local farmstead cheddar, chèvre and blue, artisan salami and ham, seasonal fruit, local honey, jam and sourdough.
hook: Everything local and in season: a board built from the farmers market, where the story behind each item is part of the flavor.
why: This board isn't a fixed list. It's a method: one cheddar, one fresh goat cheese and one adventurous cheese from local makers, a salami and a ham from a local producer, and whatever fruit is at its peak that week.
Small cards with each producer's name and town make the board a conversation, and people taste more carefully when they know where something came from.

timeline.what: Shop the market and talk to the producers.
Take out the cheeses; prep the produce.
Place the cheeses; write the labels.
Add the meats, produce, bread and condiments.
Tell the story as guests arrive.

faq.q: What is a farm-to-table charcuterie board?
faq.a: A board built from local, seasonal ingredients: cheese, meat, produce, honey and bread from nearby farms and makers.

faq.q: What if my market doesn't have local charcuterie?
faq.a: Use a local cheese or two and a good artisan salami from a regional maker. The point is in-season produce and a few local stars.

faq.q: How do you label a local board?
faq.a: Small cards with the producer's name, town and one flavor note.
